chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who heard the Sajdah (verse) being recited. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not prostrate unless he is attentive to its reciter, listening to it intently, or he is praying his prayer with the reciter. As for if he is praying in one corner and you are praying in another corner, then do not prostrate for what you have heard.'
ai.seo_question: When is prostration of recitation obligatory upon hearing a Quranic verse?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of prostration upon hearing (sajdat al-tilawah) is contingent upon the listener's attentive engagement (inbisat) with the reciter, rather than mere auditory perception. This ruling distinguishes between shared ritual presence and casual background hearing, ensuring the act remains a deliberate act of worship. The hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on intentionality and focused attention in fulfilling ritual obligations.
